newsitem.title: BRAZIL: BRAZIL DEBT OUTLOOK - No unparalleled success.
newsitem.headline: BRAZIL DEBT OUTLOOK - No unparalleled success.

text.p: Brazil on Monday priced its much-ballyhooed parallel Eurobond, finding good institutional demand but failing to take the retail market by storm, traders and co-leads said.

"We're surprised it has gone so well because the pricing only came on Friday. We have placed half of our tranche with institutional investors after expecting them to take only a quarter. The retail market should pick up soon," said an official at one of the three banks managing the deal.

ING Barings, Banque Paribas and Creditanstalt-Bankverein managed the bond, which carried a 6.625 percent coupon on each of the five-year tranches in Dutch guilders, French francs and Austrian schillings.
The coupon gave an average spread of 192 basis points over U.S. Treasuries when swapped to dollar rates, traders said.
All three tranches are fungible, or redominate into the euro when the single European currency is introduced in 1999.

Market sources said the schilling tranche appeared to have done the best, followed by the franc issue. The guilder issue was said to have done well with pension funds and other institutional investors. But market players said Dutch retail clients, which are unfamiliar with Brazil, reacted more cautiously than their counterparts in France and Austria.
Some traders said the retail market could later warm to the deal, the first of its kind by an emerging market issuer.

They noted that the average dollar-swap spread of 192 bp over U.S. Treasuries looked appealing when compared to Brazil's 8.875 percent due 2001 ZQ4P, its benchmark five-year global bond, which is now trading at 188 bp over U.S. Treasuries.

IN SECONDARY TRADE, spreads on Brazilian issues were mostly unchanged last week. Market watchers expect little in the way of new issues and say investor interest would be tamed by a series of economic indicators due out in the United States this week.
If the indicators, which include unemployment and inflation, point to increasing economic activity, it will heighten market expectations for another hike in short-term U.S. interest rates.
"It is going to be a very nervous week. Eurobond investors will be on the sidelines while the U.S. Treasury market goes crazy," said a Eurobond trader at a leading international bank in Brazil.

IN BANK ISSUES, Banco Safra's 8.375 percent due 2004 (put 1999) ZTLY looked like a cheap buy at 175 bp over when compared to three-year issues by similarly regarded bank credits Bradesco and Unibanco, traders said.
Unibanco's 8.0 percent due 2000 ZTPW is trading at 150 bp over and Bradesco's 8.0 percent due 2000 ZTCK is trading at 140 bp over.
BRAZILIAN BRADYS were not expected to get any boost from the parallel bond, which had been well publicized over the past several weeks.
Brady players said the market would keep a close eye on U.S. Treasuries and the steady flow of U.S. economic indicators due out this week.

Locally, Brazil's auction of state mining giant Vale do Rio Doce could help Brazilian Bradys if it goes through as scheduled on Tuesday, according to some players. Others, however, said the auction, even if not delayed, would be bearish on the market.
"If the auction goes ahead people will be selling after an initial pop up so the auction is actually bearish for us," said a Brady trader in New York.
